# Recorded examples

The examples on this page run in CI against these recordings from the live bridge, replayed by a stand-in bridge that answers only a call the recording fits:

- [`stats_fit_malat.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLibRust/blob/main/tests/fixtures/stats_fit_malat.json)
- [`stats_fit_limma.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLibRust/blob/main/tests/fixtures/stats_fit_limma.json)

# Same verb in other bindings

| Python (pyMzLib) | Rust (mzLibRust) | R (mzLibR) |
|---|---|---|
| `pymzlib.stats.fit` | `mzlib::stats::fit_with` with `FitOptions` | `stats_fit` |

# References

- [doi:10.2202/1544-6115.1027](https://doi.org/10.2202/1544-6115.1027): the empirical-Bayes moderated t this verb computes (Smyth, Stat Appl Genet Mol Biol 3:3, 2004)
- [doi:10.1093/nar/gkv007](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkv007): limma, whose eBayes(legacy = TRUE) mzLib reproduces to 1e-8 relative (Ritchie et al., Nucleic Acids Res 43:e47, 2015)
- [doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x): the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment in bh\_adjusted (J R Stat Soc B 57:289, 1995)

# Not yet verified

The spec lists these as open; they are reported, never hidden:

- Rust and R spellings are proposals until those bindings ship the verb.
- stats\_fit\_malat.json is the largest recorded fixture (about 258 KB): 492 features x 2 coefficients. It is real data (mzLib's RNA oligo table, \#1388), derived by a rule held in StatisticsTests.MalatDilutionFixture\_IsLog2OfMzLibsOligoTable.
